thread:
marco-support: FYI customer hitting a weird combo after 02:00 UTC — lots of 429s and 500ms+ tails. They say traffic 'falls back' to us-east and then JWT auth fails (401) on some requests. attaching logs they sent.

marco-support: log snippet:```
ts=2026-03-15T02:04:21Z req=abcd-1234 region=eu-west-1 routed_to=us-east-1 status=429 reason=rate_limit
ts=2026-03-15T02:04:22Z req=abcd-1234 routed_to=us-east-1 status=401 reason=jwt_expired token_iat=2026-03-15T01:58:00Z
```

ken-eng-routing: thanks — tagging in. do we have the x-redwood-region/x-request-id headers from the customer's client? that will confirm whether the frontend fanout happened before auth check.

elaine-cust: I can paste exact curl that reproduces:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
We set region=eu in our dashboard. at ~02:03 it starts failing. tokens were issued ~6 mins earlier.

raj-sre: Quick hypothesis: if routing falls back from eu to us-east and the edge performing auth uses a different clock or a stricter iat/exp window, tokens very close to expiry can be rejected. also retries from the client could be counted by the target region quota causing apparent double-billing.

olivia-billing: Confirming: if a request is fanout/rerouted and the target region accepts it, usage can show in that region's metering. If client retries, you can see extra token usage. we need request-ids to reconcile billing.

ken-eng-routing: There was a small routing policy change in the last rollout that relaxes affinity under load — it can send EU traffic to other zones when eu pool < 30% available. I'm checking the deploy.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T01:57Z by @ken-eng-routing -> routing-service v2.14.0. Canary 10% applied at 2026-03-15T01:58Z.

ken-eng-routing: That matches the timeframe. Can the customer share response headers from a failing request? specifically X-Redwood-Edge, X-Redwood-Region, X-Request-Id. If not, ask them to run the curl with -i.

elaine-cust: pasted a full round-trip header from a failing attempt:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 02:04:22 GMT
X-Redwood-Edge: edge-eu-11
X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1
X-Request-Id: req-20260315-xyz
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="iat in future"
```
Weird: token_iat was earlier than server time but error says iat in future.

raj-sre: "iat in future" usually means clock skew (token issuer time vs validator time). If the edge or validator's clock was ahead by a minute, a token issued earlier could be seen as future. Cross-region routing means a different validator could reject it.

ken-eng-routing: Actionable mitigation: 1) customer can set header `X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1` to force regional affinity for now; 2) we can roll back the canary if needed; 3) we can add a small grace window (±2m) on JWT validation at the edge. which do you want?

olivia-billing: Meanwhile, customers seeing retries may have incurred extra units. Please ask them to avoid aggressive client retries for 10 minutes while we investigate — we'll credit obvious double-counting after we confirm request-ids.

marco-support: customer is ok to test header pin. Elaine, can you try the curl with `-H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1" -i` and paste headers?

elaine-cust: ran it. now response headers:```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Edge: edge-eu-04
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Request-Id: req-20260315-abc
```
No 401. So header pin fixes it.

raj-sre: good repro. That confirms routing -> different validator -> clock skew. For a short-term fix I propose: a) rollback the canary to 0% until we rule out config drift; b) add ±120s skew tolerance on validators; c) trigger NTP health check across region fleet.

ken-eng-routing: I'll roll the canary back to 0% now and open an infra ticket to check NTP and validator configs.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated 2026-03-15T02:18Z by @ken-eng-routing -> routing-service v2.14.0 canary scale 0%.

olivia-billing: For billing reconciliation — please collect the failing request-ids (req-20260315-xyz etc.) and open a billing dispute with those ids attached. I'll hold credits until we validate duplicates.

marco-support: Thanks team. Next steps for support: confirm customer is unblocked by header pin or rollback, collect failing req ids, and follow up with billing. I'll update customer now. :thumbsup:

elaine-cust: thanks, pinned header worked and traffic is stable. will send req ids in DM.

raj-sre: follow-on: we should add an observability alert if auth failures spike in one region while edge shows nearby issuer timestamps skewed. filing a follow-up RFC.

ken-eng-routing: noted — will add to postmortem and follow up on routing policy thresholds.

marco-support: closing here once billing confirm credit.
